text:
incidents-bot: ALERT: Production inference errors > 5% for gpu-serve-prod (eu-west) — spike in CUDA OOM + container restarts detected. Pager sent to oncall.
leo: oncall here, investigating. what's the blast radius? any customer-facing errors showing in alerts? :eyes:
maria: seeing 502/504s and L7 timeouts in fronting ELB. Error rate spike started ~2m ago. Grafana: token errors + backend 5xx. Top model: r-infer-v2-large.
raj: logs show repeated container crashloops with exit code 137 (OOM) and driver resets: `E Cuda out of memory` across multiple pods. Autoscaler scaled from 6 -> 18 in 3 minutes then snapped back to 5; looks like oscillation.
amanda: fyi - a handful of premium customers reported latency/timeouts via support channel. ETA on impact list? we should surface to CS.
leo: @amanda please add customers list; @raj can you dump pod list + restart counts? runbook next.
raj: pod dump:
```
kubectl get pods -n inference -l svc=gpu-serve-prod -o wide
gpu-serve-prod-5a2b  CrashLoopBackOff  6 restarts  node=gpu-eu-12
gpu-serve-prod-7e1c  Running           0 restarts  node=gpu-eu-03
gpu-serve-prod-bc3d  OOMKilled         9 restarts  node=gpu-eu-04
```
Also qps per pod shows uneven distribution; some pods taking large batches -> OOM.
neal: looks like autoscaler is too aggressive on scale-up then immediately scale-down once OOM kills pods, causing thrash. We should disable scale-to-zero and add a stabilization window to prevent rapid downscaling.
maria: agree. immediate mitigations: 1) set HPA minReplicas to 6, 2) bump stabilizationWindowSeconds to 300 for scaleDown, 3) temporarily reduce targetBatchSize / maxTokens for model to prevent OOM.
leo: do we have a safe revert if config breaks?
sre-runbook-bot: Runbook: "Autoscaler oscillation causing OOM" steps
1) identify affected ASG / HPA
2) increase minReplicas
3) set scaleDown.stabilizationWindowSeconds=300
4) cordon suspect node(s) with repeated OOMs
5) roll back to CPU fallback model if GPU memory remains unstable
6) postmortem link template
raj: applying change to HPA now: `kubectl patch hpa gpu-serve-prod -p '{"spec": {"minReplicas":6}}'`
leo: patch applied. Confirm metrics for scale events.
raj: done. Also applied annotation to disable scaleToZero in autoscaler controller: `autoscaler.kubernetes.io/disable-scale-to-zero=true`
amanda: CS updated: 3 premium customers impacted (EU). Support notified and compensations queued.
neal: started cordoning node gpu-eu-04 (high OOM count) and draining pods onto other healthy nodes.
```
kubectl cordon gpu-eu-04
kubectl drain gpu-eu-04 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```
raj: drained. Some pods rescheduled and running but still seeing sporadic OOM logs on new pods with larger batches.
maria: lowering model batch size via config rollout to limit tokens per batch. `PATCH /configs/gpu-serve-prod {"max_batch_tokens": 1024}` — rolling out.
leo: slow rollout, start with 20% canary.
raj: starting canary update.
(5m passes)
raj: canary looks stable. error rate dropped from 5.8% -> 1.2% in EU region.
leo: good. now reduce autoscaler sensitivity so we don't immediately scale back down. set scaleDown.cooldown = 600s.
raj: applied cooldown 600s. Also increased eviction thresholds to prefer driver restarts over kill.
amanda: CS: customers notified of partial mitigation; latency improved but still degraded for some heavy requests. ETA for full recovery?
leo: monitoring for next 30m. If stable, we'll call incident "mitigated" and move to postmortem. Add RCA owners: raj (runtime), maria (autoscale config), leo (oncall lead).
sre-runbook-bot: Incident status updated -> MITIGATED (watching). Please fill incident template: https://runbook.internal/incidents/new
maria: note for RCA: root cause hypothesis = autoscaler oscillation + aggressive batching leading to transient node memory pressure; combined with driver resets causing OOM cascades. Mitigations in follow-up: tuning autoscaler policies, enforcing per-pod GPU memory limits, and auto-fallback to CPU model for bursts.
neal: follow-up actions created in tracker: increase min replica safety buffer for GPU pools, add a cooldown policy for autoscale controller, add metrics alert for scale oscillation (scale events > X in Y minutes), add scheduled driver update window to test stability.
leo: handoff to night oncall @maria in 10m. If errors rebound above 3% re-escalate.
amanda: logging sent to CS summary channel; customers given interim workaround (reduce concurrent batch size).
leo: thanks all. closing thread but will re-open if we see new spikes. :white_check_mark:
